## Findings
- claim-1: \(\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\) has Schur \(\mathbb Z\)-basis \(\{s_\lambda\}\), and the span \(I_{r,n-r}\) of \(s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\) is an ideal; hence \(A:=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\). [source-2@L1310-L1324|claim=formal-document]
- claim-2: For \(\rho=i^j\) and \(B=(n-r)^r\), the relevant Bruhat condition is Young-diagram containment, and \(J_v\) is generated by \(\{s_\mu:\rho\subseteq\mu\subseteq B\}\). [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]
- claim-3: Put \(\mathcal U=\{\mu:\rho\subseteq\mu\subseteq B\}\), \(F=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathcal U}\mathbb Z e_\mu\), and identify \(F\cong J_v\) by \(e_\mu\mapsto s_\mu\). For partitions \(\varnothing\ne\lambda\subseteq B\), \(\mu\in\mathcal U\), write in \(\Lambda\) \[ s_\lambda s_\mu=\sum_\nu c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}s_\nu, \] and set \[ r_{\lambda,\mu}:=\sum_{\nu\in\mathcal U}c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}e_\nu. \] Then there is an exact integral presentation \[ Q:=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong \frac{\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathcal U}\mathbb Z e_\mu} {\left\langle r_{\lambda,\mu}: \varnothing\ne\lambda\subseteq B,\ \mu\in\mathcal U\right\rangle_{\mathbb Z}}. \] Indeed, terms \(s_\nu\) with \(\nu\not\subseteq B\) vanish in \(A\), by the definition of \(I_{r,n-r}\); this is the box truncation. Since \(s_\lambda s_\mu\in J_v\) and the displayed Schur classes form the basis of \(J_v\), the surviving terms have \(\nu\in\mathcal U\). Thus the relation subgroup maps onto \(\Lambda_+J_v\). Conversely, every positive-degree element of \(A\) is a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear combination of \(s_\lambda\) with \(\varnothing\ne\lambda\subseteq B\), while every element of \(J_v\) is a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear combination of \(s_\mu\), \(\mu\in\mathcal U\). Bilinearity therefore expresses every element of \(\Lambda_+J_v\) as a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear combination of the listed products. Hence the relation subgroup is precisely \(\Lambda_+J_v\).
- claim-4: The two proposed smaller Schur generating families are \[ \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}, \qquad \{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}, \] where \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\); each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-6@L14-L42|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-5: Smith normal form of the displayed presentation matrix is expected to give \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), and hence establish irredundance of both smaller Schur families; the supplied record states that this stronger statement was not proved in the source. [source-6@L56-L72|claim=ordinary-document]
## Strategy
Let \(B=(n-r)^r\), \(\rho=i^j\), and \(\mathcal U=\{\mu:\rho\subseteq\mu\subseteq B\}\). Define
\[
S=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathcal U}\mathbb Zs_\mu\subseteq A=\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}.
\]
Using the Littlewood--Richardson support property
\[
c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}\ne0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mu\subseteq\nu,
\]
which follows because an LR tableau of coefficient \(c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}\) has skew shape \(\nu/\mu\), prove that \(S\) is an ideal: if \(\mu\in\mathcal U\), every surviving Schur term of \(s_\lambda s_\mu\) has
\(\rho\subseteq\mu\subseteq\nu\subseteq B\), hence lies in \(S\). Since \(J_v\) is generated by the \(s_\mu\) for \(\mu\in\mathcal U\), this gives
\[
J_v=S.
\]

Put \(F=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathcal U}\mathbb Ze_\mu\), and define the resulting isomorphism
\[
\phi:F\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}J_v,\qquad e_\mu\longmapsto s_\mu.
\]
For \(\varnothing\ne\lambda\subseteq B\) and \(\mu\in\mathcal U\), define
\[
r_{\lambda,\mu}=\sum_{\nu\in\mathcal U}c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}e_\nu.
\]
Box truncation implies that terms with \(\nu\not\subseteq B\) vanish in \(A\); LR support implies every nonvanishing term has \(\nu\in\mathcal U\). Therefore
\[
\phi(r_{\lambda,\mu})=s_\lambda s_\mu\in\Lambda_+J_v.
\]

Let \(R\) be the subgroup generated by the \(r_{\lambda,\mu}\). The preceding equality gives
\[
\phi(R)\subseteq\Lambda_+J_v.
\]
Conversely, positive-degree elements of \(A\) are integral combinations of \(s_\lambda\) with \(\varnothing\ne\lambda\subseteq B\), while \(J_v\) has basis \(\{s_\mu:\mu\in\mathcal U\}\). Bilinearity thus expresses every element of \(\Lambda_+J_v\) as an integral combination of \(\phi(r_{\lambda,\mu})\). Hence
\[
\phi(R)=\Lambda_+J_v,
\]
and consequently
\[
Q\cong
\frac{\displaystyle\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathcal U}\mathbb Ze_\mu}
{\displaystyle\left\langle
\sum_{\nu\in\mathcal U}c_{\lambda\mu}^{\nu}e_\nu:
\varnothing\ne\lambda\subseteq B,\ \mu\in\mathcal U
\right\rangle_{\mathbb Z}}.
\]

## Gaps
This presentation does not compute its Smith normal form. In particular, it does not prove
\[
Q\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}
\quad\text{or}\quad
\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=\binom{a+b}{a}.
\]
Thus irredundance or minimality of the two proposed smaller Schur generating families remains unresolved.

## Next
Derive a uniform Smith-normal-form calculation for the displayed LR multiplication presentation, or prove matching lower bounds for \(Q/pQ\) for every prime together with torsion-freeness.
